title: Chapter 23
content:
Jakyeong cracked his eyes open with agonizing slowness.

The sun was blazing high in the sky. After tossing and turning until the early hours of dawn, he’d only managed to catch a sliver of restless sleep once morning broke. He rolled over with a groan, but the space beside him on the sprawling mattress was completely empty.

Stretching out his stiff limbs, he sat up. Looking down, he realized someone had stripped him out of his wrecked clothes and dressed him in a set of Il-hyun's silk pajamas.

Contrary to his worst fears, Kang Il-hyun hadn't forced a brutal, full-throttle penetration last night. Grinding their hips together and holding him close had been the extent of it. Given the man’s reputation as a bloodthirsty syndicate monster, the restraint was entirely unexpected. Jakyeong had braced himself for a savage, tearing assault, yet Il-hyun’s hands and mouth had been almost disorientingly tender.

The memory left a strange, unsettled prickle in his chest.

Spending the night wound tight as a snare had left his throat bone-dry. He swung his legs out of bed and padded out into the living room, but Il-hyun was nowhere in sight.

After pouring himself a tall glass of cold water, Jakyeong began poking around the penthouse. Where the hell did the guy vanish to so early? He checked the entryway—Il-hyun's shoes were gone. Circling back, his eyes caught a neat slip of paper resting on the glass coffee table:

[Went into the office. I'll drop by around lunch.]

The handwriting was clean, elegant, and perfectly balanced. Working on a Saturday?

Honestly, it was a relief. Running into each other this morning would have made things profoundly awkward anyway.

Sipping his water, Jakyeong wandered past the curated art pieces lining the hallway until he stumbled upon a private study at the far end of the wing. Unlike Il-hyun’s fortified fortress on the outskirts, every interior door in this luxury penthouse was unlocked and open. Better yet, a quick glance confirmed there wasn't a single surveillance camera mounted to the ceiling.

The study was lined with floor-to-ceiling bookshelves. Most of the volumes were dense economic and corporate strategy texts, though a few slender books of poetry sat tucked among the spines.

Jakyeong let out a dry, involuntary scoff. Poetry. Right.

As he ran his fingers along the dark wood, he noticed the central bookcase sat on an integrated floor track. In high-end estates, sliding architectural features like this almost always meant one thing: a hidden room.

Heart rate picking up with anticipation, Jakyeong gave the heavy wood panel a firm shove. With a low, muted rumble, the entire shelving unit glided smoothly to the side, revealing a blank wall behind it.

Disappointed, he was about to slide the unit back into place when he paused, stepping closer to inspect the surface. He tapped the drywall with his knuckles. Thump, thump.

It rang completely hollow.

His eyes flared. Planting both palms flat against the panel, he applied steady lateral pressure. The wall segment slid back with a quiet hiss, revealing a concealed secondary chamber.

Jakyeong glanced over his shoulder. The penthouse was dead silent; he still had plenty of runway before lunch.

He stepped inside. The hidden room was laid out as an auxiliary private study, furnished with a minimalist desk and a row of filing cabinets. Scanning the space, Jakyeong froze.

Sitting in plain sight directly beneath the desk was a heavy digital safe.

He gave the room a rapid 360-degree sweep, checking the ceiling corners for hidden lenses. Seeing none, he knelt before the steel unit. Fortunately, this safe didn't require a biometric fingerprint—it was fitted with an electronic eight-digit keypad.

Jakyeong recalled the exact sequence Il-hyun had punched into the subterranean vault at the country mansion. He tapped the digits into the keypad one by one.

Upon pressing the final key—beep-beep-click!

A chime confirmed the lock had disengaged. Licking his dry lower lip, Jakyeong carefully pulled the heavy door open.

The moment he saw what was inside, his jaw went slack, followed by a breathless, incredulous chuckle.

"Well, look what we have here."

Neatly arranged inside the safe was a massive collection of high-capacity USB flash drives. Each drive was meticulously categorized with an embossed label showing a date and a name, laid out like merchandise in a high-end showcase. A few carried only a date, but the names on the rest read like a directory of South Korea's absolute elite—heavyweight politicians, top-tier celebrities, prominent prosecutors, and high-ranking corporate tycoons.

God only knew what kind of lethal blackmail was stored on those chips.

Pushing aside the lurid files, Jakyeong kept his eyes locked on his singular objective. His hands moved with surgical speed until his fingers suddenly halted over a matte-black drive.

It was labeled with a date from five years ago and two simple initials: DK.

Found it.

He wrapped his fingers around the drive, but hesitated to pull it from the rack. The moment this specific drive vanished, Kang Il-hyun's suspicions would lock onto him instantly.

The contract had two non-negotiable clauses: retrieve the drive, and put Kang Il-hyun in the ground. And there was still plenty of time left before the scheduled hit at the inauguration.

Jakyeong weighed the options. Take it now, or leave it for later?

He chose the path of minimum exposure. Locating the asset was half the battle won; he could simply slip back in to collect it after putting a bullet through Il-hyun’s skull.

Pulling out his encrypted phone, Jakyeong snapped high-resolution photos of the drive and its exact slot, then carefully returned it to its place. He swung the safe door shut, wiped the keypad clean of smudges, and stepped out, sliding the hidden wall and bookcase back into their flush positions.

He was strolling down the hallway when the distinct chime of the penthouse front door echoed through the foyer. Jakyeong quickly took a seat on the living room sofa, grabbing his water glass just as heavy, measured footsteps approached.

"You're finally up?"

Setting his glass down, Jakyeong turned to face him. After rolling around naked in bed together last night, the man's breezy, everyday tone was almost refreshing.

In Il-hyun’s hand was a brown paper takeout bag.

"Do you like burgers?"

Il-hyun walked over to the dining table and unbagged the meal. Jakyeong stood up and walked over. Given that he hadn't had a proper burger since landing in Korea, the smell was undeniably enticing.

"Yes... I love them."

"Good to hear. There's an artisanal burger joint on the ground concourse that makes a remarkably solid patty. Try it."

Il-hyun peeled back the foil wrapping for him and popped a straw into the cup of soda. Taking the burger, the savory aroma of charred beef and melted cheese made Jakyeong’s mouth water. He took a generous bite—the combination of fresh tomato, juicy patty, and crisp pickles was absolute perfection.

Sitting across from him, Il-hyun rested his chin on his palm, watching with an amused smile before pointing a finger at Jakyeong's face. Jakyeong skipped the napkin, simply flicking his tongue out to lick a smear of sauce from the corner of his lip.

Il-hyun’s eyes darkened slightly, tracking the movement.

"Is there something on my face?" Jakyeong asked.

"How was it?"

"It's incredible. Honestly one of the best burgers I've had in a long time."

"Not the food," Il-hyun said smoothly. "The sex last night. How was it?"

Jakyeong choked violently on his soda, narrowly avoiding spraying carbonated liquid across the mahogany table.

Cough! Hack!

Are you fucking kidding me right now?! While I'm eating?!

Dabbing his mouth frantically with a napkin, Jakyeong stared at him in utter disbelief. Il-hyun remained completely unfazed, propping his chin up as he studied the flustered reaction.

"To be completely honest," Il-hyun mused, "it hardly even qualifies as real sex."

"Why... why on earth are you asking that now...?"

"I kept my word and went gentle on you," Il-hyun murmured, a dangerous lilt in his voice. "So I was wondering if we could go again tonight."

"What?!"

The pitch of Jakyeong’s voice spiked instantly, his face pulling into a horrified scowl before he could catch himself. Wasn't this supposed to be a one-time deal?!

Judging by the steady, unblinking intensity in Il-hyun's dark pupils, the man wasn't joking in the slightest.

Jakyeong’s brain scrambled for an escape route. Flat-out refusing risked burning his access to the penthouse, but submitting to round two made his stomach turn.

"I'll... I'll think about it..."

"Alright."

Buy time, Jakyeong thought. Claim I have a fever, or fake an errand outside.

"Done thinking?"

Jakyeong’s eyes blew wide, a piece of lettuce halfway to his mouth. "Done with what?"

"You said you'd think about it."

It's been five seconds, you lunatic.

"Let me... finish eating first..."

Any remaining appetite vanished into thin air. The burger that had tasted like heaven moments ago now felt like a mouthful of dry sand. Jakyeong resorted to nibbling at a stray leaf of lettuce like a reluctant rabbit, dragging out every chew.

Il-hyun sat across from him, completely still, tracking every movement of his jaw.

Fortunately, the buzzing of Il-hyun's smartphone broke the standoff. After a terse, low-voiced exchange on the line, Il-hyun stood up and grabbed his suit jacket from the back of the chair.

"Are you leaving?" Jakyeong asked, trying not to sound too eager.

"Heading back to headquarters. We'll resume this conversation later."

An involuntary sigh of relief slipped past Jakyeong's lips.

Catching the microscopic drop in tension, Il-hyun let out a low, mocking chuckle. "Look at that. You're practically celebrating because I'm walking out the door. You're going to hurt my feelings, Yi-an."

Tossing out the playful curse with a wicked grin, Il-hyun turned and strode toward the foyer.

Flustered, Jakyeong quickly clamped his lips around the soda straw, deliberately looking away until the front door clicked shut.

Inside the abandoned public bathhouse, a single amber utility bulb flickered erratically against the damp walls.

The tiled chamber was plunged in gloomy twilight, the silence broken only by the rhythmic drip, drip of condensation falling from the ceiling pipes. In the center of the drained room, a man stripped down to his boxer briefs was bound securely to a heavy wooden chair.

The heavy metal door creaked open, allowing a brief sliver of daylight to cut through the steam before sealing shut once more.

Kang Il-hyun stepped into the gloom.

His polished leather shoes made sharp, echoing strides against the wet tile until he came to a stop before the shivering prisoner. The man looked up, his eyes swimming with absolute, primal terror.

A subordinate hurried forward, placing a folding chair behind Il-hyun. Il-hyun took a seat, drew a cigarette from his silver case, and sparked the tip.

"Well now... President Choi."

The moment the title dropped, the bound man began babbling frantic denials.

"Executive Director Kang! This is a misunderstanding! I swear on my life, I know nothing about this!"

"Why take the fall all by yourself?" Il-hyun asked, his tone deceptively mild. "Loyalty is a luxury reserved for the living, wouldn't you agree?"

Taking the calm demeanor as a sign of mercy, President Choi’s voice rose into a desperate, pleading wail. "Please believe me! I had no part in this! I'm telling the truth!"

President Choi managed one of the underground casino operations run under the Haewon Group banner. Recently, an astronomical sum of cash had been siphoned from his personal accounts. Spending his own illicit earnings wasn't an issue, but the financial pipeline the money had vanished into was deeply problematic.

A forensic sweep of Choi’s dashboard cameras and GPS route logs had yielded a clean paper trail: the cash had been hand-delivered to a private errand service specializing in untraceable wet-work. What specific contract was placed remained unknown—the office had been scrubbed clean and abandoned by the time Il-hyun's cleanup crew arrived that morning.

And most crucially: President Choi happened to be Kim Sun-young’s first cousin.

"Director Kang... please, let me speak with the Chairman!" Choi begged, tears streaming down his face. "If I could just explain this to the Chairman—!"

Without changing his expression, Il-hyun rose from his chair, stepped forward, and shoved the lit, burning end of his cigarette straight into Choi’s open mouth.

Before the man could even scream, Il-hyun’s hand clamped onto his jaw in an iron grip, shoving his entire weight backward.

SPLASH!

Still tied to the wooden chair, Choi was hurled backward into the deep communal bath basin, sinking instantly beneath the murky, standing water.

The water reached chest-high on a standing man. Instead of screams, only a frantic stream of glub-glub-glubair bubbles broke the surface as the bound man choked below.

Il-hyun stood at the edge of the pool, casually brushing a few stray water droplets off his crisp dress shirt with complete detachment.

As the frantic trail of rising bubbles thinned to an exhausted trickle, Il-hyun raised a hand, flicking two fingers toward his men.

Two enforcers stepped into the basin, seized the wooden frame, and hauled the drowning man back onto the concrete deck.

Gasp! Hack! Wheeze!

President Choi convulsed violently, coughing up lungfuls of stagnant water, his face pale as a corpse.

Il-hyun reclaimed his seat as the men dragged the sopping wet chair back into position. Placing a fresh cigarette between his lips, Il-hyun struck a match.

"See that?" he murmured, leaning forward with a gentle, terrifying smile. "That's what happens when you lie to me."

A subordinate rushed over with a dry towel. Il-hyun took it and began methodically, almost tenderly, drying the water and sweat from Choi’s bruised face.

"The only person in this world who can grant you your life right now... isn't my father. It's me," Il-hyun whispered, his voice dropping into a razor-sharp growl. "Think carefully before you open your mouth again. Keep crying for the Chairman, and you're going to put me in a foul fucking mood. Understood?"

Translator's Notes (A/N):

  • Errand Centers / Shadow Fixers (심부름센터 / 흥신소): In South Korea, simbureum-center (errand agencies) operate in a legal gray area, ranging from mundane private detective work to shady underground fixers who broker illicit tracking, debt collection, and contract operations for wealthy clients.

  • Underworld Discipline in Bathhouses (목욕탕 심문): Abandoned public bathhouses (mogyoktang) are classic noir venues in Korean crime fiction, offering built-in soundproofing, drains for blood, and deep communal pools (tang) used for waterboarding and coercion without leaving forensic traces outside.
